character.lede: A teal lap-siding colonial with black shutters and flower boxes has taupe-brick gables over the garage and entry. A walled stone terrace holds the pool, a swing set and a sandbox.

spots.line: A media credenza, a wall screen and a sofa fill the den.
A house bed, a toy box and an easel fill Mateo's room.
A fireplace and a chesterfield sofa warm the living room.

facts.style: Two-storey teal lap-siding colonial with taupe-brick garage and entry gables, a hipped roof with a big front cross gable and a nested bay gable, black louvred shutters and flower boxes, a low hipped east wing; warm taupe-and-cherry fireside interior; walled stone pool terrace

character.truths: The Core sits on a shelf in the Living Room. Television in the Den and the Family Room. The kitchen has a breakfast bar. Pool, swing set, sandbox and garden beds on a walled stone terrace.

details.rule: every beat of an adult or teen persona (13 or older) gets a detail (before, after, steps, fact); pair beats first

yuvomi: [note] Stored in SQLite on your Core. CalDAV and CardDAV sync are optional.
one household planner, not an account per person
already in the persona pool: share cap risk
paperless: [note] AI features are off by default. If you turn them on they can use a local model.
[note] Office document conversion is not wired up in this build; OCR and archiving of PDFs and scans works.
baikal: Whoever opens the app first runs the install wizard and sets the admin password
Overlaps Radicale and Nextcloud calendars: one calendar server per household
jellyfin: [note] Plays your own files. Say that, not "Netflix".
[claims] Do not say it plays copyrighted material from anywhere.
Plays your own media only: never "streams any movie".
QA capture is the setup wizard with a container id as the server name; the gallery frame is a demo library with lurid exploitation film posters: neither usable.
donetick: [cloud-link] Notifications use Telegram or Pushover. Both are outside services.
NFC-tag completion needs a phone that reads NFC on the home network
vaultwarden: [note] Bitwarden-compatible server, unofficial. Do not say "Bitwarden".
project-nomad: [public-access] Ships without authentication. For trusted home networks only. Never describe it as exposed.
[note] amd64 only (fine on the Core). Internet is needed once for setup and downloads.
[claims] Educational content comes from third-party sources. Do not promise grades.
Ships without authentication: home network only, never described as exposed.
Needs the internet once for setup and downloads; never "fully offline" or "anywhere".
libretranslate: [note] Works offline once language models are downloaded.
Listing says "works fully offline": banned wording (sec-offline)
Likely already heavy in the existing stories
excalidraw: [note] amd64 only. An Excalidraw MCP entry exists for agents.
marketplace: Manifest source points to ozencb/excalidraw-persist, a 105-star wrapper, not excalidraw/excalidraw.
librephotos: [note] First setup takes 5 to 10 minutes while models and migrations start.
[note] No API is mentioned in the listing; treat as web interface only for agent purposes.
Face recognition is sensitive: say what it does, never that it "knows" people
Overlaps Immich; use it to relieve Immich's share
blockbench: Projects live in the browser (IndexedDB) or in files the person saves: the Core serves the app, it does not hold the models
The listing names Minecraft models; say "game models" or "block models" in copy
Free-text store claim "never sees your models" is accurate for the container
gitea: [note] Gitea Mirror is a different listing (it copies GitHub repositories into Gitea). Name only Gitea. Forgejo does the same job; name one Git host per household.
[note] The listing mentions Actions CI. The package ships the forge and its database only, no runner, so do not show a CI run.
[claims] Say where the repositories are (on the Core). Do not say it syncs with, or is compatible with, GitHub.
Listing mentions Actions CI; no runner ships: never show a CI run.
Gitea Mirror is a different app.
lunalytics: Setup wizard asks for email and username on first visit
Do not claim a public status page
Overlaps Uptime Kuma (another slice): one uptime monitor per household
adguardhome: [note] Overlaps Pi-hole; pick one per story.
[claims] Same as Pi-hole: no parental-control promise.
[qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
Listing mentions adult-content parental controls: never repeat it (sec-safety-people)
hortusfox: Do not say it keeps plants alive
Plant health alerts and a public gallery exist: keep the gallery off in a story
adventurelog: [qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
n8n: [licence] Fair-code licence, not open source. Say "source-available"; do not say "open source".
[note] An n8n MCP entry exists for agents.
Fair-code licence: say source-available, never open source.
Public URL setting is for webhooks; leave off the scene.
Listing says full control over data: connectors to cloud services still pass data to them.
opencode: [cloud-link] The Hub wires it to the Core's local model by default (hub_integration inference). The app can also connect to cloud providers with a key you add inside it; leave that off. A coding agent is private only on
[claims] Never claim parity with a hosted coding model and never a speed figure. The agent edits files, so the beat shows the person approving the change (agents prepare, people approve).
[note] The web interface has no sign-in unless a server password is set at install. The older OpenCode Web listing is superseded; name only OpenCode.
[note] Added 2026-10-15 for the builder archetype: the old cloud-or-developer exclusion lumped it with apps that need cloud keys; this one is wired to the local model.
[qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
habitica: The sign-up page in the capture carries a cookie-consent banner: check the self-hosted build for analytics scripts before saying it sends nothing out
Game, not a health or behaviour tool: no outcomes
rembg: [note] amd64 only (fine on the Core). REST API available.
[qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
amd64 only; CPU inference; models are cached after the first download (internet).
No QA screenshot and no gallery image at all: needs a capture.
tldraw: not open source (tldraw licence; a production watermark shows)
librespeed: Say "the link to the Core" or "the Wi-Fi in this room"; never "internet speed"
No speed figures in copy (num rules): show the act, not a number
Listing says "privacy-focused" and "no tracking": do not repeat
blinko: [qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
AI search and chat need a model provider added in the app (OpenAI, Ollama, LiteLLM...): not wired by the Hub.
No QA run; gallery frame is upstream marketing with a "#Password" tagged note and a gmail file name: reject.
Companion desktop and mobile clients are separate downloads.
privatebin: Footer of the screen says the server has "zero knowledge": do not repeat
Overlaps Cryptgeon and Enclosed: one per household
